So we're a small startup, three engineers, and we need to build the backend API for our appointment booking product, we sell to barbershops and small salons. The shops set up their services and staff and opening hours, and then their customers book slots on a little booking page, and the shop gets a calendar view. The hard part is the availability logic, like staff have shifts, services have durations and buffer times, some services need a specific chair or room, and double booking absolutely cannot happen, that's the one thing that kills trust instantly. Um, we expect maybe two hundred shops in the first year, each with what, a few dozen bookings a day, so the traffic is small, but reliability matters because booking happens when the shop is closed too, evenings, weekends. We need SMS confirmations to customers, we already picked Twilio for that. Payments come later, not in the first version, but we know it's coming so don't paint us into a corner. The mobile app team starts in a month and they need a stable API to build against, so the API shape matters more than the implementation, we can swap internals later. We deploy on AWS, that's already decided company-wide, and we have CI/CD set up with GitHub Actions. Oh and audit logs, shops will call support saying a booking vanished, we need to be able to see exactly what happened.
